affected_system: multichannel public-service intake, triage, dispatch, and resolution workflow
alternatives: compare eligible treated and credible untreated units for phased public-service channel and routing redesign
estimate pre-specified overall and distributional effects of phased public-service channel and routing redesign
pair staggered queue or service-area evaluation with outcome panels with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Requests, contacts, duplicates, service categories, assignments, work orders, and outcomes remain distinct.
Channel and area comparisons account for taxonomy, access, publication, and reporting differences.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain pre-intervention conditions for phased public-service channel and routing redesign.

constraints.description: The 311 and public-service demand operations evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: chief service officer and 311 operations director
decision_question: Did phased channel and routing changes reduce verified resident effort and workflow delay without exclusion?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The 311 and public-service demand operations evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
independence_key.decision_object: phased public-service channel and routing redesign
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for phased public-service channel and routing redesign passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: staggered queue or service-area evaluation with outcome panels
independence_key.primary_outcome: change in verified end-to-end handling time and repeat contact

intended_claim: A versioned evaluate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting phased public-service channel and routing redesign, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: change in verified end-to-end handling time and repeat contact
distributional gap in change in verified end-to-end handling time and repeat contact
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer resident welfare, satisfaction, or causal resolution from closure codes alone.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for phased public-service channel and routing redesign passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.

title: Evaluate service intake and routing redesign
